records.quote: The vat contained an acid powerful enough to destroy anything--except gold. In fact, the vat itself had to be lined with gold-leaf. I knew that in twenty-four hours there wouldn't be a recognizable body left, and in a week there wouldn't be anything at all.
records.paraphrase: Gregg explains the properties of an acid strong enough to dissolve everything but gold, used to eliminate the body.

records.quote: It is a physiological absurdity--it contradicts the laws of natural science.
records.paraphrase: Gregg frames what he witnessed as contradicting known natural laws.

records.quote: For hours at a time I've watched the change.... Did you ever see a body decompose? Of course not! Neither have I. But you must know in a general way what the process is. Well, this has been the exact opposite!
records.paraphrase: Gregg describes observing a reverse of decomposition occurring in the vat.

records.quote: I watched the coming of hair, a yellow tangle of it sprouting from the bare round skull, until--oh, God!--the flesh began making itself before my eyes!
records.paraphrase: Hair and flesh regenerate on the reforming body as Gregg watches.

records.quote: I replaced the lid. I spent a week convincing myself that it was all impossible, that I _couldn't_ have seen anything of the sort. Then I went to the vat again----
records.paraphrase: Gregg repeatedly returns to observe and test whether what he saw was real.

records.quote: Every night lately he heard the same peculiar noise somewhere in this wing of the building.... Like a body groaning and turning in restless sleep, it was. It scared him.
records.paraphrase: The watchman is frightened by recurring groaning sounds in the building.

records.quote: The loud click was the cocking of the revolver.
records.paraphrase: Gregg cocks a revolver, leading to his suicide.

records.quote: I've watched her limbs grow rosy! Her lips are scarlet! Her eyes are bright--they opened yesterday--and her breasts were rising and falling--oh, almost imperceptibly--but that was last night.
records.paraphrase: The body progressively returns to life, showing color, open eyes, and breathing.

records.quote: First, I stared at the heap of grave-mold as it shaped itself into _bones_, a skeleton.
records.paraphrase: The dissolved remains reform into a skeleton.

records.quote: Asa Gregg was blind ... had been, since that night three years past when the acid splashed....
records.paraphrase: The ending reveals Gregg had been blind for years, undercutting the reliability of what he described seeing.

records.quote:
Soon she's going to get out of that vat!_" Gregg bleated.
"Jeannette, forgive me--God, forgive me--but I will not--I cannot--I dare not stay here to see her then!
records.paraphrase: Terrified of the reviving body emerging, Gregg refuses to remain.

records.quote: The stuff utterly dissolves animal tissue, bone, even the common ores--keeps them in suspension.
records.paraphrase: The acid is described as dissolving tissue, bone, and ores, keeping them in suspension.

criteria.rationale: The story invokes chemical properties of an acid dissolving tissue and ores, and explicitly frames events against the laws of natural science. However, the central marvel (reverse decomposition) is presented as a physiological absurdity and is finally undercut as the delusion of a blind man, so the scientific framing is used to signal impossibility rather than to develop genuine science.

The gold-lined acid vat is an engineered chemical apparatus specifically designed to dissolve a body without a trace, and it materially drives the plot (the disposal of the corpse and the supposed resurrection). It is more than a mere mention, though it functions as a chemical setting rather than a novel invention.
The narrative is set in the author's contemporary present with no speculative future, remote past, or temporal displacement.

No consequences are systematically extrapolated from an identifiable scientific or social premise; the reverse-decomposition marvel is explicitly labeled impossible and is revealed as hallucination, so no coherent extrapolative logic is developed.

Gregg repeatedly returns to observe the vat over nights and spends a week trying to convince himself the phenomenon is impossible, which resembles observation and evidential testing. But this is the obsessive checking of a hallucinating blind man, not genuine systematic inquiry driving valid understanding, so materiality and interpretation are uncertain.
There are no other planets, dimensions, nonordinary cosmic environments, or visitors from them; the setting is an ordinary chemical company office.
The events are a murder and a suicide, personal misfortunes without large-scale disaster dimension; there is no natural, technological, cosmic, biological, or human-caused catastrophe of broad scale.

candidates.description: A gold-dissolution-resistant acid vat in which a murdered body, instead of dissolving, undergoes reverse decomposition-reconstituting from grave-mold into skeleton, hair, flesh, and finally a reviving living woman.

novelty.rationale: The purported world-altering reversal of decomposition is never established as an actual difference in the story universe. The frame explicitly frames it as impossible and contradicting natural law, and the closing revelation that Gregg had been blind for three years discloses that the entire 'resurrection' was hallucinated by a guilt-ridden, blind murderer. No totalizing empirical difference is validated in the storyworld; the story resolves into psychological horror, not an altered universe.

cognitive_validation.rationale: The acid itself has a mundane pseudo-chemical rationale, but the central phenomenon-reverse decomposition and revival-is given no coherent, systematic, immanent nonsupernatural account. It is presented as a 'physiological absurdity' contradicting natural law, and the ending reframes it as a hallucination rather than an operating imaginary science. There is no immanent logic governing the reversal.

narrative_hegemony.rationale: The apparent reversal/revival drives the entire confessional narrative arc and directly causes Gregg's terror and suicide, so as an experienced phenomenon it dominates the narrative logic-though it is ultimately a delusion rather than a validated novum.

estrangement.rationale: Reader-facing contrast is drawn between ordinary decomposition and its impossible reversal (ev03), then upended by the revelation of Gregg's blindness (ev11), reframing the horror as subjective delusion rather than an estranging cognitive novelty.

candidates.description: An industrial acid powerful enough to dissolve all animal tissue, bone, and common ores except gold, requiring a gold-leaf-lined vat, used to eliminate a murder victim.

novelty.rationale: A potent dissolving acid is at most an unusual plot device, not a totalizing or world-altering difference from the empirical norm. It does not change the story universe or any crucial aspect of it.

cognitive_validation.rationale: The acid is given a plausible, coherent, nonsupernatural chemical rationale (dissolves tissue/bone/ores, keeps them in suspension, resisted only by gold, hence gold-lined vat).

narrative_hegemony.rationale: The acid is an incidental instrument of body disposal; it enables the plot but does not determine the overriding narrative logic, which is the psychological horror of guilt and the hallucinated revival.

estrangement.rationale: The acid provides a minor technical contrast with ordinary chemistry but serves only as a disposal tool, generating no sustained estrangement of the story universe.
